clue.text: Interrogator who knows all the answers!

definitions.text: Interrogator who knows all the answers!

parts.words: Interrogator who knows all the answers!
parts.note: reads like a sinister police questioner, but it is the host of a trivia contest who holds the answer cards

explanation.surface: A fearsome interrogator who is never surprised by anything a suspect says.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark warns that the 'interrogator' is a cheerful games host, not a detective: he asks the questions and has every answer on a card.
explanation.definitionFit: The host of a quiz asks the questions and holds the correct replies, so he knows them all.

clue.text: Not right to doubt the heifer is Scottish

indicators.note: Not tells us the letter for right is to be left out of the doubt word

parts.note: a doubt is a query

explanation.surface: Uncertainty about whether a young cow comes from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' removes R from QUERY. 'is Scottish' tells you the answer is a Scots word: a quey is a young cow in Scottish dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect this is a young cow that has not yet calved.

clue.text: In a small mouthful, I'd found there was little taste

parts.note: taken as written
a sip is a small mouthful of drink
the contraction gives its letters with no apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tiny sip and finds the drink rather bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bland or flavourless has very little taste.

clue.text: A tender marine at sea in the sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentle marine sailor on a voyage across the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the letters of A TENDER MARINE; 'the sea' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the large sea lying between southern Europe and North Africa.

clue.text: Namely the said winter runner is allowed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are to be spoken and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a ski is a runner used on winter snow, and licit means allowed, so together SKI LICIT

explanation.surface: A skier asks whether winter runners are permitted, as just mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: SKI plus LICIT, said aloud, sounds like the Latin word. 'the said' is filler linking the parts. Scilicet is the Latin behind the abbreviation 'sc.'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin adverb means 'that is to say', used to introduce an explanation.

clue.text: Monkey in game reserve some are watching closely

indicators.note: the clue words hold back a few of their letters in sequence, which is where the answer sits

explanation.surface: Visitors to a wildlife park keep a close watch on a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across monkEY IN Game. 'game reserve' looks like one surface phrase but 'reserve some' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be looking at something carefully is to be keeping a close watch on it.

clue.text: It is made to last

parts.note: sounds like something built durable, but a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler shapes footwear around

explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like the verb 'endure'; it is the cobbler's wooden foot form.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is fashioned around a cobbler's last, a wooden model of a foot.

clue.text: Impetuous description of Etna

parts.note: a hasty, rash person is described by the phrase that literally fits a volcano with a burning summit

explanation.surface: A fiery epithet for the Sicilian volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily, so its summit is literally hot; the same phrase names a rash person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, quick-tempered person is called this, and a volcano's summit is literally hot.

clue.text: A realisation when one is at the bank?

definitions.text: A realisation when one is at the bank?

parts.words: A realisation when one is at the bank?
parts.note: suggests a sudden insight by a riverbank, but realisation here means converting an asset into money at a bank

explanation.walkthrough: 'realisation' in finance means turning something into money; you do it at a bank, not on a river bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting a cheque or bond into money is the financial sense of realising it.

clue.text: Relaxed, having stopped a hundred short

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the letter for a hundred is missing

parts.note: to have stopped is to have ceased
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone calmed down after just failing to reach a century.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loosened or made less tense has been slackened off.

clue.text: It is silly to hold mother in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: to hold means the silly word wraps round the word for mother

parts.note: silly means idiotic
MA is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: It is foolish to grip your mother in a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is' is filler for the surface. 'to hold' puts MA inside IDIOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Language that follows the natural phrasing of native speakers is in their characteristic way of talking.

clue.text: Petition early in the day

parts.note: a request made before noon, which is the church service of devotions held at the start of the day

explanation.surface: A request lodged first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Matins, the Anglican morning office, is often called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican service of matins is a set of devotions said in the morning.

clue.text: Placing vegetables on grassy areas

parts.note: placing means putting
greens are leafy green vegetables

explanation.surface: Laying out cabbages on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf course has smooth, closely mown grass patches round each hole where the ball is tapped in.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course these are the closely mown turf surfaces round each hole.

clue.text: Stuffing not replaced on bear

parts.note: stuffing is padding

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soft toy whose stuffing has not been put back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges NOT to TON. Paddington is the famous fictional bear from Peru, named after a London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is a well-known fictional bear in children's books.

clue.text: More senior-sounding civic dignitaries

parts.note: town council members whose title, said aloud, resembles a phrase for men who are older

explanation.walkthrough: The title, spoken, is close to 'older men', which suits the senior members of a town council.
explanation.definitionFit: These are senior elected members of an English borough or city council.

clue.text: In India, demanded a rich head-covering

indicators.note: In shows the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In India someone asks for an expensive hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across IndIA DEManded.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crown or headband is an ornate band worn on the head.

clue.text: Crack made by Rev A Ship in church

indicators.note: in places the clergyman, A and ship inside the letters for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written: the abbreviation for Reverend
SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship

explanation.surface: A vicar called Ship cracks something in his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev A Ship' reads as a clergyman's name; it is REV, A and SS placed inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep fissure in a glacier is a crack in the ice.

clue.text: Lower the dignity of French fellow going round the point

parts.note: DE is French for of

indicators.note: going round means the fellow word encircles the point

parts.note: a fellow is a man
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Insulting a Frenchman who turns about a compass direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French fellow' looks like one idea; it is 'of French' (DE) then 'fellow' (MAN), which 'going round' puts around E.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble or degrade someone is to cause them a loss of standing.

clue.text: For a short time rave about the goddess

parts.note: MIN, minute, is a short time

indicators.note: about means around and out of order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone raves briefly about a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges RAVE to ERVA. Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman deity of wisdom and crafts.

clue.text: Clever enough to get on at the resort

parts.note: clever enough means bright
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone smart enough to board the train at the seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a popular seaside town on England's south coast.

clue.text: In that place neither moved round

indicators.note: moved round means the letters of neither are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Nobody in that place budged.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means within that thing or location.

clue.text: It may have rhyme but not reason

definitions.text: It may have rhyme but not reason

parts.words: It may have rhyme but not reason
parts.note: plays on the idiom 'neither rhyme nor reason': poetry that rhymes but makes no sense

explanation.walkthrough: The clue twists the idiom 'without rhyme or reason' to describe absurd poems like Lear's limericks.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's comic poems rhyme neatly while making no sense at all.

clue.text: Take one's food on the wing?

definitions.text: Take one's food on the wing?

parts.words: Take one's food on the wing?
parts.note: a bird of prey dives through the air to snatch its meal while flying

explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wing' means in flight; a hawk dives to seize its prey without landing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey dives down suddenly through the air to seize its quarry.

clue.text: Striking in vain?

definitions.meaning: workers on strike are not working
a threat or boast made in vain is empty and pointless

explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like 'impressive'; here it means on strike, so not working.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers on strike are inactive, and an empty threat is pointless and without effect.

clue.text: Despotic turn, say, on eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tyrannical twist, so to speak, on something odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruel and oppressive ruler behaves like a tyrant.

clue.text: Surrender produce

definitions.meaning: to give in or give way
a crop or return, as in a field's harvest

explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' can be noun or verb; either fits.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way is to capitulate, and a harvest or financial return is an output.

clue.text: In the Tyne a predictable tide

indicators.note: In shows the answer is tucked inside the following words

explanation.surface: On the River Tyne the tides come and go on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across tyNE A Predictable. The Tyne is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap is the tide of least range, occurring at the moon's first and third quarters.

clue.text: One might turn up to put one in

definitions.text: One might turn up to put one in

parts.words: One might turn up to put one in
parts.note: plays on the idiom 'put in' a brief showing at an event: arriving is how you make one

explanation.walkthrough: To 'put in an appearance' is to attend briefly; turning up is exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at an event to be seen there is a brief showing of oneself.
